context: Fortuno and Grisselda Dibbs are a worried, doting couple in a wartime camp who treat their hound, Biscotti, like a child — Fortuno is especially protective and forbids strangers from petting him. They’re relieved animals are permitted in camp because it keeps Biscotti away from the dangers and anxieties of the fighting. Grisselda sometimes chides Fortuno for being brusque with outsiders, while Fortuno interprets strangers’ looks as attempts to touch the dog. The player is an outsider whose comments range from complimenting the hound to teasing Fortuno about his presumption.
